sourceChecks.title: Neuronal cell loss accompanies the brain tissue response to chronically implanted silicon microelectrode arrays
sourceChecks.excerpt: We observed persistent ED1 immunoreactivity around implanted silicon microelectrode arrays
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In adult rat cortex, implanted arrays were associated with persistent inflammatory immunoreactivity and lower nearby nerve-fiber and neuronal-body density; the authors relate this response to chronic recording failure.
sourceChecks.limitations: Animal preclinical study; no human millions-neuron read/write interface, decades of stability, or absence of foreign-body response.

sourceChecks.title: The unexpected sight: improvement of visual function following intracortical microstimulation of the human occipital cortex
sourceChecks.excerpt: Although our results are based on a single case
sourceChecks.paraphrase: One of four implanted participants, with bilateral NAION and residual pupillary response, had unexpected improvement in natural vision after stimulation experiments began. Authors discuss possible spontaneous recovery; this uncontrolled case cannot establish causality or predictable restoration.
sourceChecks.limitations: No general efficacy, durable normal vision, color/motion restoration across patients, or retinal/optic nerve regeneration established; case mechanism remains uncertain.

sourceChecks.title: Effect of Nonmyeloablative Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation vs Continued Disease-Modifying Therapy on Disease Progression in Patients With Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis
sourceChecks.excerpt: Disease progression occurred in 3 patients in the HSCT group and 34 patients in the DMT group.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Randomized 110-patient relapsing-remitting MS study reported progression in 3 HSCT versus 34 DMT patients, with median follow-up two years; authors call for replication and long-term safety study.
sourceChecks.limitations: This is a selected disease subgroup and a treatment comparison; it does not demonstrate safe one-time cure, CNS-wide complete remyelination, axonal restoration, or absence of broad immunosuppression.

sourceChecks.title: Tau pathology in the medial temporal lobe of athletes with chronic traumatic encephalopathy: a chronic effects of neurotrauma consortium study
sourceChecks.excerpt: We examined MTL tissue obtained from 40 male Caucasian and African American athletes
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The authors examined postmortem medial temporal lobe tissue from 40 athletes with CTE and found tau profiles varied by pathological stage, suggesting candidate markers of progression.
sourceChecks.limitations: Postmortem characterization does not establish the complete causal pathway, an in-life diagnostic, or a treatment that reverses established CTE or restores cognition.

sourceChecks.title: Cortical circuit principles predict patterns of trauma induced tauopathy in humans
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Independent reopen returned only HHS disclosure footer; no inspectable title or research passage, so this preprint is not used as positive backing.
sourceChecks.limitations: Preprint and postmortem correlation; no established upstream trigger or therapeutic reversal.

items.corrections: A root cause and one-time reversal therapy for established Alzheimer disease/tauopathies was not demonstrated by this bounded audit. The relevant phase 3 trial page was found but inaccessible.

Specific human neurostimulation/neuroprosthesis studies for motor-complete injury were found, but their articles could not be read in this audit; no full spinal-cord regeneration claim is substantiated.
A randomized trial examined autologous HSCT as an immune-reset strategy for highly active relapsing-remitting MS. It does not establish a safe complete cure or full CNS remyelination.

Rat implant-response experiment documents persistent inflammation and adjacent neuronal loss, explicitly identifying an unresolved mechanism of chronic recording failure. It supports the biocompatibility research challenge, not long-lived zero-response interface performance.

A 40-athlete postmortem CTE study characterizes stage-associated tau distribution and clinical-history correlations. The second preprint page could not be independently read and is excluded; no causal closure or reversal is demonstrated.

The bounded search did not locate an inspectable primary result for a universal acute-stroke neuroprotectant producing near-zero infarct volume. No such efficacy or the downstream impact forecast is supported here.

A randomized trial of responsive thalamic stimulation for drug-resistant generalized epilepsy was found but the primary page was blocked. No permanent non-destructive cure was established by readable evidence.

A primary single-patient report describes improved residual visual function during a cortical-stimulation study after optic-nerve injury. This unexpected case does not show predictable restoration or near-normal vision.
The bounded search did not substantiate a single transdiagnostic autism mechanism that can be safely normalized in all individuals or a cure after childhood. The impact claim remains unsubstantiated.

The bounded search found no inspectable primary result establishing one pathway that reverses neuronal loss across Parkinson disease, ALS, and FTD. Cross-disease reversal and impact are unsupported here.

notes: All four retained positive URLs independently reopened and passages matched; the fifth preprint reopen yielded footer only, removed from positive backing.
NRL-04 changed to goal-supported because implant-response study investigates inflammation/failure, not a new functional stable interface capability.
Visual improvement is uncontrolled unexpected association in one participant; spontaneous recovery and patient-specific substrate remain possible.
Every evidence.supportedClaim names only the single-page finding, with exact universal/impact claims retained separately.
